prompt: Customers sign up for back-in-stock alerts on product pages and receive email notifications when inventory is replenished; you view all signups and sent notifications in one admin dashboard.

intent.desiredOutcome: Customers sign up for back-in-stock alerts on product pages and receive email notifications when inventory is replenished; you view all signups and sent notifications in one admin dashboard.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version keeps the admin page responsive even with hundreds of signups and notifications logged. Include filters or sorting by product or date so the merchant can quickly find what they need. Show clear timestamps for each notification sent so the merchant knows when customers were notified. Test edge cases: duplicate signups, products that go out of stock again before customers receive the email, and bulk inventory updates. The two views (signups vs. sent notifications) should be distinct and easy to switch between.

plan.dataFlow: A customer submits their email on the storefront widget for a specific out-of-stock product variant, creating a pending signup record. When an inventory replenishment event fires, the system reads all pending signups for the restocked variant and fetches the variant's display details. For each signup, it sends a restock notification email, records the outcome in the notification log, and transitions the signup to notified. If inventory drops to zero again before processing completes, in-flight sends are allowed to complete but any remaining pending signups stay pending until the next replenishment event. The admin dashboard provides two independently filterable views: all signups (by product or date) and all sent notifications (by product or date), both backed by their respective persistence tables.

triggers.event: inventory level for a product variant increases to a positive quantity
triggers.idempotency: If the same inventory replenishment event is delivered more than once for the same variant, signups already in a terminal state are skipped and no duplicate emails are sent.

capabilities.description: Fetch the product variant's display name and product title to populate the notification email and widget confirmation.
Persist a customer's email address alongside the product variant they wish to be alerted about.
Determine whether a customer email is already registered for alerts on a given variant to prevent duplicate signups.
Retrieve all pending signups associated with a specific product variant when a restock event fires.
Confirm that the restocked quantity is genuinely positive before dispatching any notifications.
Deliver a back-in-stock email to a customer containing the product variant details and a link to purchase.
Log the result of each notification attempt, including timestamp and success or failure, against the originating signup.
Return a filterable, sortable list of all alert signups for the admin dashboard.
Return a filterable, sortable list of all notification log entries for the admin dashboard.
Cancel a pending signup at merchant request, transitioning it to cancelled so no future notification is sent.

persistence.name: alert_signups
persistence.purpose: Stores each customer's request to be notified when a specific product variant returns to stock, and tracks its lifecycle state.

columns.name: product_variant_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the out-of-stock variant the customer wants to be alerted about

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the parent product for filtering in the admin dashboard

persistence.keyedBy: one row per unique combination of customer email and product variant external identifier

persistence.name: notification_log
persistence.purpose: Immutable audit record of every notification send attempt, including outcome and timestamp, linked to the originating signup.

columns.name: signup_id
columns.purpose: links the log entry to the alert signup that generated it

columns.name: product_variant_external_id
columns.purpose: denormalized variant reference to support admin filtering without joining signups

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: denormalized product reference to support admin filtering without joining signups

persistence.keyedBy: one row per notification send attempt, keyed by its own surrogate identifier

transitions.trigger: restock notification successfully sent to customer
merchant removes the signup via the admin dashboard

invariants: Exactly one row exists per customer email and product variant combination; a second signup for the same pair is rejected as a duplicate.
A row in 'notified' or 'cancelled' never returns to 'pending'.
A notification log entry is created before the signup row transitions to 'notified'; partial writes that skip logging are not permitted.
Only rows in 'pending' status are eligible for notification dispatch.

externalContracts.purpose: Register a customer's email address for a back-in-stock alert on a specific product variant.
Check whether a given email is already registered for alerts on a specific product variant so the widget can suppress the form.
Return a paginated, filterable list of all alert signups for the merchant dashboard signups view.
Return a paginated, filterable list of all sent notification log entries for the merchant dashboard notifications view.
Cancel a pending signup so the customer will not receive a notification for this variant.

edgeCases: A customer submits the signup form twice for the same variant — the second request must be silently rejected as a no-op without creating a duplicate record.

The product variant's inventory drops back to zero between the restock event firing and the notification emails being dispatched — emails already sent are kept; remaining pending signups stay pending and will be processed on the next replenishment event.
A bulk inventory update restocks multiple variants simultaneously, generating concurrent restock events — each variant's pending signups must be processed independently without cross-contamination.

The customer's email address is undeliverable and the send attempt fails — the signup must remain in 'pending' state, the failed attempt must be recorded in the notification log with a failure outcome, and no transition to 'notified' occurs.

A product variant is deleted in the storefront before its pending signups are processed — the system must skip notification dispatch for orphaned signups and record them as cancelled rather than leaving them permanently pending.

Two concurrent deliveries of the same inventory replenishment event attempt to process the same batch of pending signups — only one delivery should succeed in transitioning each signup to 'notified'; the second must treat already-transitioned rows as no-ops.
